source_review.methods_review: Publisher primary HTML Section2.3, Sections3.1.5,3.1.6 and3.1.12; original Table1 cruise windows and Table2 depth cells checked against PDF pixels.
source_review.read_method: Existing read-only OOXML parser preserving original cells and row numbers.
source_review.identity_review: Explicit group-row mappings for Florida, North Brazil at11S and upper Labrador only. No automatic inheritance to systems, families, Guiana or deep components.

references.range_interpretation: Vertical depth extent of the source-selected inverse-transport domain. Not temporal variation, uncertainty or a uniform thickness.
references.geographic_scope: North Brazil Current 11∘ S; publisher longitude limits -35.7:-34.7 degrees east. Nominal section latitude is not an exact boundary-station coordinate.
references.temporal_scope: Whole-section sampling window 1994-04-01 to 1994-05-07; inverse-model group 1990–1999. Cruise snapshot, not a decade mean.
references.source_definition: Vertical domain selected by net mass transport integrated over the chosen station pairs with the same flow direction (Section2.3); reported metre depths of selected neutral-density layers.
references.source_locator: Table2 original XLSX row45, group row44, E(layer indices), F(depth in m); Table1 row5; Sections2.3 and 3.1.5.
references.qualification: Source-selected inverse-transport domain, not uniform thickness or a closed cross-section. No same-source width record is joined; existing width observations have different sources and scope. Uses the paper North Brazil label specifically at11S; no Guiana or family inheritance. Nominal source latitude is retained even where Table1 gives a broader section band. Transport uncertainty is not depth error.
